front: Paris est plus grand que Lyon.
pronunciation: [pah-REE eh plü GRAHN kuh lee-OHN]
back: Paris is bigger than Lyon.

front: Le train est moins cher que l'avion.
pronunciation: [luh TRAN eh mwan SHEHR kuh lah-VYOHN]
back: The train is cheaper than the plane.

front: Ma sœur est aussi grande que moi.
pronunciation: [mah suhr eh toh-see GRAHND kuh MWAH]
back: My sister is as tall as me.
context: Aussi + adjective + que = as… as. Stressed pronoun after que: moi, toi, lui.

front: Il est plus âgé que moi de trois ans.
pronunciation: [ee leh plü zah-ZHAY kuh MWAH duh trwah ZAHN]
back: He's three years older than me.
context: 'De' introduces the difference: de trois ans.

front: Ce restaurant est meilleur que l'autre.
pronunciation: [suh res-toh-RAHN eh meh-YUHR kuh LOH-truh]
back: This restaurant is better than the other one.

front: Elle chante mieux que son frère.
pronunciation: [el shahnt MYUH kuh sohn FREHR]
back: She sings better than her brother.
context: Bien (adverb) → mieux. 'Meilleur' qualifies a noun; 'mieux' qualifies a verb.

front: Je me sens mieux aujourd'hui.
pronunciation: [zhuh muh sahn MYUH oh-zhoor-DWEE]
back: I feel better today.

front: Ce film est pire que le premier.
pronunciation: [suh feelm eh PEER kuh luh pruh-MYAY]
back: This film is worse than the first one.
context: Mauvais → pire (or 'plus mauvais'). Mal → pis is rare; use 'plus mal'.

front: Il travaille plus que moi.
pronunciation: [eel trah-vahy PLÜS kuh MWAH]
back: He works more than me.
context: With verbs: verb + plus/moins/autant + que. 'Plus' is pronounced [plüs] here.

front: Je lis autant que toi.
pronunciation: [zhuh lee oh-TAHN kuh TWAH]
back: I read as much as you.

front: Il y a plus de touristes en été qu'en hiver.
pronunciation: [eel yah plü duh too-REEST ahn nay-TAY kahn nee-VEHR]
back: There are more tourists in summer than in winter.
context: With nouns: plus de / moins de / autant de + noun + que.

front: J'ai moins de temps libre qu'avant.
pronunciation: [zhay mwan duh tahn LEE-bruh kah-VAHN]
back: I have less free time than before.

front: Nous avons autant de travail que vous.
pronunciation: [noo zah-vohn oh-tahn duh trah-VAHY kuh VOO]
back: We have as much work as you.

front: La vie est plus chère à Paris qu'en province.
pronunciation: [lah vee eh plü SHEHR ah pah-REE kahn proh-VANS]
back: Life is more expensive in Paris than in the provinces.
context: 'La province' = everywhere in France outside Paris.

front: C'est de plus en plus difficile de trouver un logement.
pronunciation: [seh duh plü zahn plü dee-fee-SEEL duh troo-vay an lozh-MAHN]
back: It's harder and harder to find housing.
context: 'De plus en plus' = more and more; 'de moins en moins' = less and less.

front: Plus je travaille, plus je suis fatigué.
pronunciation: [plü zhuh trah-VAHY, plü zhuh swee fah-tee-GAY]
back: The more I work, the more tired I am.

front: Moins on dort, moins on est efficace.
pronunciation: [mwan zohn DOR, mwan zohn neh teh-fee-KAS]
back: The less you sleep, the less efficient you are.

front: Il est deux fois plus rapide que moi.
pronunciation: [ee leh duh fwah plü rah-PEED kuh MWAH]
back: He's twice as fast as me.

front: Ce n'est pas aussi simple que ça.
pronunciation: [suh neh pah zoh-see SAN-pluh kuh SAH]
back: It's not as simple as that.
context: In negative comparisons, 'si' can replace 'aussi': pas si simple.

front: Elle est bien plus intelligente que lui.
pronunciation: [el eh byan plü zan-teh-lee-ZHAHNT kuh LWEE]
back: She's much more intelligent than him.

front: Ton appartement est un peu plus petit que le mien.
pronunciation: [tohn nah-par-tuh-mahn eh tan puh plü puh-TEE kuh luh MYAN]
back: Your apartment is a bit smaller than mine.

front: Le français est différent de l'espagnol.
pronunciation: [luh frahn-SEH eh dee-fay-rahn duh les-pan-YOL]
back: French is different from Spanish.

front: Mon téléphone est le même que le tien.
pronunciation: [mohn tay-lay-fun eh luh mem kuh luh TYAN]
back: My phone is the same as yours.

front: Ce vin ressemble à un bordeaux.
pronunciation: [suh van ruh-sahm-bluh ah an bor-DOH]
back: This wine is like a Bordeaux.

front: Il ressemble beaucoup à son père.
pronunciation: [eel ruh-sahm-bluh boh-koo ah sohn PEHR]
back: He looks a lot like his father.
context: 'Ressembler à' takes an indirect object: il lui ressemble.

front: Par rapport à l'année dernière, les prix ont augmenté.
pronunciation: [par rah-por ah lah-nay dehr-NYEHR, lay pree ohn tohg-mahn-TAY]
back: Compared to last year, prices have gone up.

front: Comparé à Londres, Paris semble petit.
pronunciation: [kohm-pah-ray ah LOHN-druh, pah-REE sahm-bluh puh-TEE]
back: Compared to London, Paris seems small.

front: Je préfère le train à la voiture.
pronunciation: [zhuh pray-fehr luh tran ah lah vwah-TÜR]
back: I prefer the train to the car.

front: Elle parle aussi bien anglais qu'espagnol.
pronunciation: [el parl oh-see byan nahn-GLEH kes-pan-YOL]
back: She speaks English as well as Spanish.

front: Ce n'est pas mieux, c'est pareil.
pronunciation: [suh neh pah MYUH, seh pah-RAY]
back: It's not better, it's the same.

front: Les deux options se valent.
pronunciation: [lay duh zop-syohn suh VAHL]
back: The two options are equally good.

front: C'est plus facile à dire qu'à faire.
pronunciation: [seh plü fah-SEEL ah deer kah FEHR]
back: It's easier said than done.

front: Mieux vaut tard que jamais.
pronunciation: [myuh voh TAR kuh zhah-MEH]
back: Better late than never.
context: Proverb with 'mieux vaut' = it's better to.

front: Elle court plus vite que tout le monde.
pronunciation: [el koor plü VEET kuh tool MOHND]
back: She runs faster than everyone.

front: La situation est bien pire qu'on ne le pensait.
pronunciation: [lah see-tü-ah-syohn eh byan PEER kohn nuh luh pahn-SEH]
back: The situation is much worse than we thought.
context: Formal 'ne explétif' after a comparison: 'qu'on ne le pensait' (it doesn't make the sentence negative).
